title: How Sweet to Bless the Lord
description: How Sweet to Bless the Lord in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 30 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Pleasures of Spiritual Worship”, where the book credits them to Urwick's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How sweet to bless the Lord, And in his prais-es join, With saints his good-ness to re-cord, And sing his power di-vine!

lines: How sweet to bless the Lord,
With saints his goodness to record,
Like rays of pure, celestial light,
While rich supplies of Jesus' grace

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
